executive_summary: This report identifies recurring style signals across 25 collected items from 12 public web sources. The strongest repeated themes are sheer layering, softened tailoring, and continued interest in archival feminine styling. Coverage is primarily editorial, so the report reflects style media discourse rather than retail sales or broad consumer adoption.

top_signals.name: Sheer layering
top_signals.evidence: Repeated references to transparent fabrics, mesh, organza, and layered styling across editorial sources.
top_signals.index_note: Signal appears strongest in eveningwear and transitional styling contexts.

top_signals.name: Soft tailoring
top_signals.evidence: Recurring mentions of relaxed suiting, oversized blazers, and structured silhouettes with softened proportions.
top_signals.index_note: Signal overlaps with officewear and minimal luxury language.

top_signals.name: Archival romanticism
top_signals.evidence: References to lace, bows, vintage femininity, and historical styling cues appeared across multiple sources.
top_signals.index_note: Signal requires further tracking before classification as sustained.

limitations: Coverage is skewed toward editorial sources and may not reflect retail sales data.
Social platform signals are limited in this collection window and classified as high-noise.
Sample size is small relative to the full scope of public style discourse.
confidence_notes: Confidence reflects recurrence and source diversity, not popularity or sales data.
volatility_notes: Social-origin signals are treated as volatile by default unless corroborated by non-social sources across multiple reporting periods.
incentive_notes: Editorial sources are not treated as neutral; coverage may be shaped by commerce and PR incentives.
human_editor_note: Placeholder example report used to scaffold the archive and report page templates.
